rationale: This is a bare two-way MIN of two textbook anomaly ranks (operating profitability à la Novy-Marx/Ball et al. and R&D intensity à la Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) with no new economic content beyond "screen on both," and the MIN operator makes the score effectively equal to whichever known anomaly happens to be weaker, which is a screening rule rather than a mechanism.

Internally consistent, but it is a cosmetic re-parameterization of Proposal 1 (R&D intensity × profitability) using a lag, cash flow instead of accruals-based income, and an R&D-capitalized denominator — the R&D-adjusted asset base is a modest improvement, yet the signal remains a product of two known anomaly ranks and is largely redundant with the rest of this batch.

The first leg is literally Novy-Marx gross profitability, and the second leg pools organically-generated intangibles with acquisition goodwill, which carry opposite return implications (goodwill loads on asset growth/overpayment and predicts negatively), so the intangible conditioner is economically muddled rather than sharpening the profitability effect.

The explicit difference between capitalized-R&D profitability and reported profitability is a genuine measurement-error construct rather than another rank of R&D intensity, and the interaction with reported profitability is well motivated — though note the uplift term is mechanically decreasing in ROA (a high-ROA firm is diluted by adding the R&D stock to assets), so the two legs are negatively related by construction and the test should confirm the surviving long leg is not just mid-ROA firms.

A three-way MIN stacks the profitability level, the profitability trend (itself a known ROE/profitability-change effect), and R&D intensity into a signal whose value is determined by whichever rank is lowest, which dilutes the intended interaction, and the MA(3)+LAG+TREND(5) chain will materially depress coverage and bias toward long-lived survivors.

The expression matches the stated hypothesis and sign, but it is simply the short-leg mirror of Proposals 1–2 (R&D intensity × low cash profitability) and is close to the established cash-profitability/distress result, with the added risk that the R&D literature documents *positive* abnormal returns for exactly these high-R&D, currently-unprofitable firms, so the expected sign is contestable rather than novel.
